peer_critiques.critique: FATAL, and it is the test rather than the thesis. The thesis — the system has a demand problem and every proposal treats demand as solved — is right, and adversary:P2's beeond measurement is the most useful number any room produced. But P4's separating experiment is: wire design.js, wait seven days of ordinary work, count invocations; still zero means the diagnosis is demand and the whole §8 agenda is aimed at the wrong thing. The confound sits inside the adversary's own document: adversary:P2 measured that ordinary work on this machine IS harness work — 2026-08-31, eight beeond commits, all eight harness; 172 session files, one touching a venture. So seven days of ordinary work is seven days in which no design task is scheduled, and a zero measures the absence of design WORK, not the absence of design DEMAND. The treatment and the confound are the same variable. Run as specified it returns zero with near-certainty and licenses a conclusion it did not earn, and by build-order step 5 that conclusion gates the entire company's build order behind an IF AND ONLY IF. This is the mirror image of the defect my own P14 refuses in the first mission: an exit that cannot fail informatively, versus one that cannot fail at all. FOR THE POSITION TO SURVIVE, one of two things must be true: (1) the seven days must contain at least one task that cannot complete without a design pass — which means the test FOLLOWS a mission rather than gating it, reversing the adversary's own ordering, and that real cost is why this is fatal rather than serious; or (2) the inference is demoted from dispositive to informative, using the discipline visionary:P11 already wrote for this exact shape — 'a finding, never an automatic action' — and the IF AND ONLY IF in build-order step 5 is deleted. I prefer (2) because it is free, and note that it also rescues adversary's build-order step 1, whose third metric (one unsolicited human response) is readable at n=1 and is rung 1 of the evidence ladder. The tripwire in step 2 is the only mechanism anyone proposed that would make the experiment actually happen and it belongs in the plan regardless.

SERIOUS. The position insists the outbound wrapper ships as ONE artifact carrying all four properties — dry-run default, hash-bound send, named-human register, rate ceiling — because they share a code path and shipping three of four ships a gap. The unit is unbuildable today by the risk-modeler's own two other statements: open question 3 says every rate ceiling needs a number and 'I will not invent one', and the refuse list forbids a budget: field that nothing counts. So one of the four properties is blocked on a founder decision nobody has made, and writing it before the number exists is refused by the same document — which makes the whole wrapper hostage to a missing number. Repair: ship the three that are buildable and make the fourth a DECLARED BLOCK with clearable_by: a daily dollar ceiling from the founder. That is the blocked-row shape my P3 half depends on, and it turns 'we are waiting on a person' from an omission into a record. Serious rather than fatal because the ordering claim the position actually defends — the wrapper before inbound — survives intact and I agree with it.

SERIOUS, and deliberately not a restatement of the concession the visionary already made honestly in its own counter. Rungs 0-1 are not the flywheel turning slowly; they are a DIFFERENT INSTRUMENT. A rung-1 result and a rung-4 result recorded in the same field with only a rung: annotation to separate them is how 'a stranger understood it' gets reported as 'someone paid' — and the world verifier that P1 puts everything downstream of is precisely what consumes that field. N1 (union, never average) has been applied to judge panels by four of five personas and by NOBODY to the evidence ladder, where the same failure is available and more consequential. Repair: rung: is mandatory on every done-test and the ladder REFUSES aggregation across rungs — a schema refusal in the same shape as refusing a summed total in a judge output.

SERIOUS, and about the input rather than the idea. The founder-preference corpus is good and it is the one proposal creating a store outside the four STARTUP-OS §6 declares, which my P7 refuses — but the stronger objection is measured. Preference pairs are written only when the founder picks A over B, and the only place that happens is the balcony: 7 views, 1 that acts, and an escalation Inbox empty on every project ever. The visionary's own what_must_be_true concedes the dependency — 'no input if the balcony surfaces no forks' — but treats the balcony's EXISTENCE as the precondition. The measurement says the precondition is a balcony that has been USED, which is a different and unmet thing. Repair: P5 is downstream of a measured balcony action, which is P9's N, now doing work for two positions.

MINOR, and it is agreement with an addition. The measurement that the birth certificate exists four times with four exemption conventions is the most useful single finding for my lane, because it condemned my own P3 under my own N4. The addition: the four exemption conventions differ in a way that matters to the anti-roadmap, and unused_reason's shape (a 40-character length floor plus a fails-when-used rule) is the only one that makes an exemption COST something to write. Converge the other three on that shape, not on a new one — an exemption that is cheap to write is how a refusal decays into a formality.

MINOR, and the adversary half-names the tension itself. P1 says the harness sits on the three-week abandonment curve and a 24/7 loop yields more dead projects reached faster; P12 refuses the 'tenth attempt' framing and establishes that nothing here failed in the ordinary sense; the counter concedes that 'a prerequisite is not a project — it does not have to beat an abandonment base rate'. Those cannot all be load-bearing at once, and in my reading P12 is the one that survives. Minor because refusing a framing you were handed and recording why is the most credible act any persona performed in Round 1, and because P1's underlying measurement (eleven projects over twenty commits, nine dead) is sound and useful whatever it is taken to prove.

remaining_dissent.holds_because: Cheap to reverse is not cheap to carry. architect:P12 sorts the bill of materials by cost-to-reverse and concludes the reversible half — packs, personas, council, board, missions file, balcony views, FIELDS — should be built 'fast, loose and continuously'. Reversibility is a property of ONE CHANGE; carrying cost is a property of the ACCUMULATED SET, and the sort collapses two different axes. Every artifact in adversary:P6's supersession record was in the cheap reversible half — the session-file count superseded five times, the suite denominator four, the .qa count twice, the branch name five, the main sha four times in one day — each individually trivial to fix, each fixed repeatedly, and the aggregate is a 637-line document whose main content is corrections to itself. Nothing in that record was hard to reverse and all of it was expensive to hold. The architect's own evidence points away from the architect's conclusion: the roster reached 26 agents one cheap reversible file at a time, the collapse to 7 was correct and expensive, and architect:P11 says the pack shape re-runs that multiplication. 'Fast and loose on the reversible half' is a description of how the last nine phases were built; it produced 48 check steps and one venture task, and not one of the 48 was hard to reverse. I am not arguing for slow — speed belongs on the MISSION side and the ceiling belongs on the ARTIFACT side, and 'reversible' is the wrong predicate for deciding which is which. The right predicate is the one visionary:P14 reached independently: flywheel, feeder, or inventory. Inventory that is cheap to delete is still inventory while it is held.

The hook's scope rule is right for the founder and wrong for the loop, and the distinguishing variable is unrecorded. risk-modeler:P2 refuses to widen pre-tool-use.sh over the founder's own user-scope MCP servers, on the grounds that this repo should not govern the founder's Gmail during the founder's own interactive session and that widening is the inverted #96.3 resolution CLAUDE.md warns about. For an interactive session that is exactly right and I agree. The loop is not an interactive session — the entire premise is that it runs while the founder sleeps — so 'the founder's own session' is the wrong frame for a 3am dispatch that inherits those servers. The risk-modeler's own open question 4 records that at least one live dispatch path carried tiktok_publish, sandbox_exec, Gmail send and an authenticated Chrome to an agent no repo file granted them, and its own P14 item 8 names the founder as a single point of failure for every human gate — which the scope rule silently assumes is present. Confirmed today: the PreToolUse matcher is Bash|Edit|Write|NotebookEdit|mcp__ so the call DOES reach the hook, and mcp-policy.json governs two servers (playwright, claim-append) in mode: shadow, neither of them the dangerous one. My P1 claims the smallest company cannot reach a stranger; today it can; and the layer that would stop it has been declared out of scope for a reason that holds only in the case that is not the dangerous one. The answer is neither 'widen the hook' nor 'leave it alone' — it is that who initiated the session is a fact nothing records.

'Trust last' is not 'trust never', and last is how things get built. visionary:P1's reasoning sequences trust behind the world's verdict, citing T1's own note that it is downstream and cannot be built first, and the visionary's build order places it eighth and forced-last. I refuse it for year one outright, and the difference is not scheduling: open-source.md §16 records that nothing across 177 surveyed repositories implements worker trust — highest cost, least precedent in the entire catalogue — and the architecture REMOVES THE SUBJECT, because fresh context per move plus a pack that is a grant and a stop means there is no persistent worker for trust to accrue to. What varies between two dispatches is the grant, and the grant is already the security boundary. Gap #10 is not deferred, it is ANSWERED, and an answered gap should leave the list rather than sit at the bottom of it where a quiet month will promote it.

No done-test may be resolved by the producing model, and all four rooms that state it cite the same 0.543-against-a-0.741-self-consistent-panel measurement. adversary:P8 does not dispute the rule — it accepts the reasoning and attacks the consequence (an unbounded stream of per-pack founder approvals on the critical path of a system premised on human absence), which is a different and live disagreement. Supported by strategist:P14 and risk-modeler:P5, which state it inside a numbered position, plus the architect's and the visionary's refuse lists, which carry it outside one.

Union, never average: no score summed from judge outputs anywhere, and design.js's total field is the named live instance of the defect. Supported by visionary:P7, which names design.js's summed total directly, and strategist:P1, whose 'cannot judge quality' row rests on the same measurement, plus the architect's and the risk-modeler's refuse lists.

One risk classifier, extended and never paralleled — including by a small helper answering 'is this outbound?'. Re-derived today: the classifier's public surface is classifyFile/classifyFiles and its only input is a normalised path string. Supported by strategist:P6 (N4), visionary:P11, architect:P6, risk-modeler:P1.

No outbound spend before a rate limit exists that something enforces; money is the one axis this repo's vocabulary cannot express, because every tier it has is about reversibility or blast radius. Supported by strategist:P10, visionary:P12, risk-modeler:P7, adversary:P10.

blocking-human by TYPE is what makes 24/7 safe rather than by policy, it is already built as the only structural impossibility in the tree, and it has zero consumers that route an act through it. Supported by strategist:P1 (N8), visionary:P9, risk-modeler:P4.

Built-and-never-wired must be prevented at merge rather than detected afterwards, and the predicate must be built once rather than a fifth time. Supported by visionary:P10, risk-modeler:P3, architect:P8, strategist:P3 — with adversary:P4 dissenting that it is a demand signal misread as an engineering defect. Convergence on the mechanism, live disagreement on what its output proves.

Every persona independently confessed, from a sealed room, that its own proposal is too large: risk-modeler's counter concedes 'three controls, not thirteen'; adversary refuses 'any new mechanism before the demand test, including mechanisms I would otherwise support'; architect's counter concedes 'a founder can read my build order as phase ten'; visionary classifies most of the repo as inventory; strategist's counter conceded fourteen stopping mechanisms. Five rooms, no cross-visibility, one shape. It is the board's strongest finding and it is about the board — and the support for it sits in each persona's strongest_counter field rather than in any numbered position, which is itself the point: not one of the five proposed the mechanism that would have caught what all five confessed.

strongest_counter: Five sealed rooms independently confessed that their own proposals were too large, and my answer to that is another filter — a ceiling whose only job is to bound mechanisms. The count is better than it was: nine of my fourteen positions build nothing, and after folding P3 into the architect's predicate and downgrading P5 to a labelled policy, three of my positions are mechanisms rather than five. A refusal has no caller, cannot become unwired, needs no expiry check to keep working, and in visionary:P14's vocabulary is negative inventory. But adversary:P6 landed the objection I did not anticipate and cannot close. A refusal costs nothing to RUN and it does cost something to HOLD: someone must consult the list before proposing, and `.out-of-scope/` in CI checks a MERGE, not a PROPOSAL. The filtering conversation — a board meeting exactly like this one — is where the cost of a refusal is actually paid, and it is precisely where no mechanism reaches. Moving the expiry from calendar to counter reduces the carrying cost; it does not put a mechanism on the proposal. Worse, and this is the part I would not want a synthesizer to soften: my Round-1 P1 described seven capabilities the smallest company 'cannot' have, and risk-modeler:P2 measured that three of them are live right now — outbound mail, publishing and remote execution all return exit 0 from the only blocking hook, and the blocking-human gate that would stop them has no consumer. I wrote an intended system in the present tense. That is the identical defect as prose describing enforcement that does not exist, which is the defect this repository was built to catch, committed by the persona whose entire job is to catch it. If the board discounts my positions by one notch on that basis it is entitled to. The second objection I still cannot mechanise is the one from Round 1: STARTUP-OS §1b already concluded the rebuild is small, so if most of the remaining work is WIRING then a refusal-heavy posture is fighting a war already won, and adversary's demand test — repaired to a finding rather than a gate — would settle in seven days what this meeting has spent five rooms arguing.
